title: RedSan: A Redundant Memory Instruction Sanitizer for GPU Programs
problem: Existing GPU profiling tools focus on hotspot identification but miss opportunities for removing redundant instructions in already-optimized CUDA programs.
motivation: Redundant memory operations are common even in production-grade code; identifying and eliminating them could unlock significant performance gains beyond standard profiling.
method: The tool works by inserting monitoring code into compiled CUDA programs to track every memory operation—both loads (reading data) and stores (writing data)—as the program runs, without requiring access to the original source code. It identifies when the same data is loaded multiple times unnecessarily or when data is stored but never used, marking these as redundant operations. The method was validated on standard performance benchmarks: PolybenchGPU, Rodinia, PASTA, DARKNET, and LULESH.
key_novelty: It's the first tool to use binary instrumentation (monitoring how compiled CUDA code actually runs, without source files) to find and eliminate redundant memory operations, achieving over 6× speedup by catching inefficiencies that existing profilers miss.
contributions: RedSan binary instrumentation profiler for redundant memory detection
Actionable optimization guidance beyond hotspot analysis
6.27× speedup and 3× memory instruction reduction on benchmarks
Demonstrated effectiveness on both compute-bound and memory-bound kernels
limitations: Overhead of binary instrumentation not detailed; limited discussion of how to automate redundancy elimination; evaluation on standard benchmarks may not reflect production codes.
primary_theme: Identifying redundant memory operations in optimized GPU code
